saw_lines: Men don’t browse skincare. They buy the one thing that fixes what bugs them, then stick with it.
So the sale happens in the first line of the ad. Whoever names the problem first gets the click.
13 of your 65 live ads lead with the Botox hook. The other 52 don’t. Put the problem and the offer up front in every ad.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active US ads, 9 Oct 2026
points: 13 of 65 live ads open on the same “did you get Botox” story, so they now compete for the same people. The price angle (“Kinda expensive”) is a second strong hook with only a few variations.
The “Kinda expensive” ad shows an amber jar, while the site sells a black one. One ad says 23,146 men, 38 others say 470,000+ jars. Keep product and proof identical everywhere.
The offer sits below the cut
The median ad is 167 words, the longest 636. Buy one get one and the 90 day guarantee come last, after “See more”. Put them in the first two lines and on the creative.
Meta limits 5 ads for some audiences. Lines like “skin looks 5 to 10 years younger” and “rebuilds collagen at the cellular level” are what review flags. Say what customers noticed instead.
